title: Streamlined Security Request Playbook and Tiering Matrix
creator: Sofia Morales
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a high volume of non-bug compliance requests (SOC2/ISO evidence, HIPAA questionnaires, GDPR/DPA clauses, and third-party vendor questionnaires). Triage today is ad hoc across Solutions, SE, and Product — leading to slow SLAs, duplicated effort, missed requirements in contracts, and poor predictability for sales.

Goal: Define a single playbook and a 3-tier prioritization matrix for security & compliance requests that standardizes intake routing, ownership, expected SLAs, and escalation paths. The playbook must cover: (1) automated intake fields, (2) decision criteria to map requests to Tier 1/2/3, (3) required artifact owners (legal, security, eng), (4) templates and canned answers for common questionnaire items, and (5) feedback loop to update product docs and roadmap.

Scope: Non-bug compliance requests only (vendor questionnaires, SOC2/ISO evidence requests, DPA addendums, HIPAA scoping clarifications, GDPR data processing questions). Excludes infra-level remediations that require engineering projects (those are routed to ENG via existing incident/feature flow).
acceptance_criteria: A documented playbook with step-by-step routing for incoming requests hosted in Confluence
A 3-tier prioritization matrix with clear decision rules and SLA targets (T1: 48h, T2: 10 business days, T3: 30 business days)
Automated intake form in Zendesk / Intercom that captures the fields required by the playbook
Ownership matrix mapping request types to roles (SE, Security, Legal, Product, Eng)
A small canonical response library (top 40 questionnaire items) drafted and reviewed by Security/Legal
Pilot run with 3 active enterprise customers and documented cycle time improvement compared to baseline
proposal: 1) Create a concise Confluence playbook that operationalizes routing rules and owner checklists. 2) Build a triage decision matrix (Tier 1/2/3) with explicit criteria: scope (PII/PHI impact), required engineering changes, contractual change requests, and legal sign-off needs. 3) Implement a lightweight intake form (Zendesk/Intercom) that tags requests and auto-assigns to a Triage queue. 4) Ship a first-draft response library and run a 4-week pilot with Solutions Engineering and two sales-managed enterprise customers. 5) Iterate and bake into Support/SE playbooks and the Console help center.
decisions: Adopt 3-tier model rather than 4+ tiers to keep routing simple for small SE team
SLA targets agreed: T1 48 hours, T2 10 business days, T3 30 business days
Security and Legal will sign off on the canonical responses before pilot
Automated intake will be implemented in Zendesk initially (not a full custom portal) to iterate quickly
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: Over-automation could misclassify complex requests—mitigation: manual review fallback and 'escalate to security' flag
Tradeoff: Short SLAs for T1 may burden Security team during peak—mitigation: cap T1 volume via qualification rules and use SE for pre-triage
Risk: Canonical responses may leak product constraints—mitigation: legal-approved templates and product review before publishing
